Parameters of the three-trophic-level eco-evolutionary model

Source: R/food_web.R
food_web_params.Rd

Collects the parameters of food_web_dynamics(), named as in chapter 3 of McPeek (2017), with the values of its figure 3.2 for the resource and the consumer and of its figure 3.11 (bidirectional-dependent traits) for the predator. Greek letters are spelt out and the optima are prefixed with z: zc_R is the trait value at which the intrinsic birth rate of the resource is highest, zf_N and zx_P the values at which the intrinsic death rates of the consumer and the predator are lowest.

Usage

food_web_params(
  c0 = 1,
  gamma = 0.002,
  zc_R = 10,
  d = 0.02,
  a0 = 0.1,
  b = 0.1,
  h = 0.1,
  f0 = 0.1,
  theta = 0.01,
  zf_N = 4,
  g = 0,
  m0 = 0.05,
  n = 0.1,
  l = 0.1,
  v0 = 0.001,
  w = 0.1,
  u = 0.1,
  x0 = 0.01,
  delta = 0.01,
  zx_P = 1,
  y = 0,
  beta = 5,
  phi = 5,
  psi = 5,
  alpha = 0.1,
  rho = 0.1,
  tau = 0.1,
  eps_R = 20,
  eps_N = 20,
  eta_N = 20,
  eta_P = 20,
  kappa_R = 20,
  kappa_P = 20
)

Arguments

c0, gamma, zc_R

Maximum intrinsic birth rate of the resource, the strength of stabilizing selection on it and its optimum.

d

Density-dependent death rate of the resource.

a0, b, h

Maximum attack coefficient, conversion efficiency and handling time of the consumer feeding on the resource.

f0, theta, zf_N

Minimum intrinsic death rate of the consumer, the strength of stabilizing selection on it and its optimum.

g

Density-dependent death rate of the consumer.

m0, n, l

Maximum attack coefficient, conversion efficiency and handling time of the predator feeding on the consumer.

v0, w, u

The same for the predator feeding on the resource, used only with omnivory = TRUE.

x0, delta, zx_P

Minimum intrinsic death rate of the predator, the strength of stabilizing selection on it and its optimum.

y

Density-dependent death rate of the predator.

beta, phi, psi

Widths of the Gaussian attack coefficients of the consumer on the resource, the predator on the consumer and the predator on the resource.

alpha, rho, tau

Steepnesses of the logistic attack coefficients, in the same order.

eps_R, eps_N, eta_N, eta_P, kappa_R, kappa_P

Half-saturation constants of the Michaelis-Menten attack coefficients: of the resource and consumer traits for the consumer on the resource, of the consumer and predator traits for the predator on the consumer, and of the resource and predator traits for the predator on the resource.

Value

A named list of class food_web_params.

Details

The intrinsic rates are quadratic in the traits (equations 3.12, 3.13 and 3.21): \(c(z_R) = c_0 (1 - \gamma (z_R - zc_R)^2)\), \(f(z_N) = f_0 (1 + \theta (z_N - zf_N)^2)\) and \(x(z_P) = x_0 (1 + \delta (z_P - zx_P)^2)\). Each feeding link has an attack coefficient with a maximum (a0 for the consumer on the resource, m0 for the predator on the consumer, v0 for the predator on the resource) and a parameter that sets the strength of selection on it, which one depends on the attack form chosen in food_web_dynamics():

  • "gaussian" (bidirectional-dependent traits, equation 3.16 and box 3.1): the attack coefficient is highest when the traits match and declines as \(a_0 \exp(-((z_N - z_R) / \beta)^2)\); the widths are beta, phi and psi.

  • "logistic" (unidirectional-dependent traits, equation 3.15): the attack coefficient rises with the difference between the traits of the consumer and its prey, as \(a_0 / (1 + \exp(-\alpha (z_N - z_R)))\); the steepnesses are alpha, rho and tau.

  • "michaelis" (unidirectional-independent traits, equation 3.14): each trait raises the attack coefficient on its own, as \(a_0 \, z_R / (\epsilon_R + z_R) \cdot z_N / (\epsilon_N + z_N)\); the half-saturation constants are eps_R and eps_N, eta_N and eta_P, kappa_R and kappa_P. Traits must then be positive.

References

McPeek, M. A. (2017). Evolutionary Community Ecology. Princeton University Press. doi:10.23943/princeton/9780691088778.001.0001

See also

food_web_dynamics()

Examples

p <- food_web_params(c0 = 10, d = 0.2)
p$c0
#> [1] 10
